title: The lightkeepers
text: Bell Rock lighthouse, {{1}} stands on a reef {{2}} the tide exposes the rock for only a few hours at a time, was built by the engineer Robert Stevenson between 1807 and 1811. Conditions were {{3}} dangerous that masons could work only at low water, and the tower, lit {{4}} the first time in 1811, took four years to complete. It {{5}} guided shipping ever since without a single structural failure. Robert belonged to a family {{6}} members designed most of Scotland's lighthouses for over a century and a half. The lights were originally kept {{7}} teams of resident keepers, and the last of them left in 1998, {{8}} automation finally replaced the human watch.

gaps.hint: relative: lighthouse, ___ stands on a reef
gaps.explanation: Non-defining relative after the comma; 'that' is impossible here.

gaps.hint: relative adverb: a reef ___ the tide exposes
gaps.explanation: 'Where' refers back to the reef as the place.
'So dangerous that' — degree plus result clause.

gaps.hint: preposition: lit ___ the first time in 1811
gaps.explanation: 'For the first time' is the fixed phrase.

gaps.hint: auxiliary: it ___ guided shipping ever since
gaps.explanation: Present perfect with 'ever since': has guided.
'Whose' links the family to its members.
Passive agent: the keepers did the keeping, so 'by'.
Non-defining time clause after the year.
